funder: Saskatchewan Lotteries Trust Fund — administered by Sask Sport / SaskCulture / SPRA
amount_notes: Minimum $250 for southern communities, $500 for northern communities. Maximum not publicly stated — determined by community population formula. Grants over $2,000 require portion allocated to under-represented populations including Indigenous people.
organization_types_eligible: Non-profit community organizations operated by volunteers in Saskatchewan
Organizations eligible via designation by Minister of Parks Culture and Sport
First Nation communities and northern settlements may apply directly
Municipal governments administer grants to local non-profit groups
eligibility_criteria: Must be a non-profit volunteer-led community organization in Saskatchewan
Must be designated eligible by Minister of Parks Culture and Sport OR apply through municipality or First Nation
Projects must develop sport, culture, or recreation programs for Saskatchewan residents
Grants over $2,000 must allocate portion to under-represented populations including Indigenous people
Projects must serve local community needs
exclusions: Organizations not designated or applying through eligible municipality or First Nation
Projects not related to sport, culture, or recreation
time_sensitive_note: Community-specific deadlines vary. Some communities deadline April 15 2026 — verify Langenburg SK intake immediately. Projects April 1 2026 to March 31 2027. Contact Town of Langenburg or nearest First Nation to confirm local intake status. Indigenous people are a priority population — strong fit for Emerge Academy.
notes: ACCESS PATH FOR EMERGE ACADEMY: Apply through Town of Langenburg or a Treaty 4 First Nation community as the municipal/First Nation intake point. Emerge Academy as an NFP would receive funding through the community intake rather than directly. Alternatively apply through Sask Sport as a member organization once incorporated. Over 1,200 organizations receive direct funding through this system — it is the primary sport funding mechanism in Saskatchewan. Indigenous people explicitly listed as priority population.
